claude_code.how: For on-demand compression, run headroom mcp install, then start/restart Claude Code and verify the MCP tools. Upstream exposes headroom_compress, headroom_retrieve and headroom_stats without requiring a proxy. Automatic traffic compression is a different, optional route using headroom proxy and explicit client routing to that proxy.

codex.how: Use Codex's native stdio MCP registration with command headroom and args [mcp, serve]; add --proxy-url only to identify a deliberately selected proxy. Upstream's MCP-host instructions explicitly support Codex and do not require mcporter between Codex and Headroom.

official_baseline_claims.claim: The v0.39.1 README's seeded, offline proof table reports 17199 -> 13597 tokens (21%) for code search, 55957 -> 24340 (57%) for SRE incident debugging, 58801 -> 33895 (42%) for codebase exploration, and 46067 -> 32429 (30%) for GitHub issue triage. These are upstream benchmark scenarios measured with its provider tokenizer and shipped compress(), not the host's measured cards.

Upstream says repeated JSON arrays and logs can exceed 90% compression, while prose and already-dense output compress little; it directs users to their own savings measurements rather than presenting one universal compression rate.

limitations.text: On-demand MCP compression happens after the LLM receives content, and its calls/results themselves enter session context. A smaller compression response is therefore not automatically the complete workflow or provider-billing reduction; retrieval costs and repeated subagent interactions matter.

headroom_compress requires a content string and returns a retrieval hash. The documented local original-content TTL is one hour; proxy storage normally expires after 30 minutes, configurable via HEADROOM_CCR_TTL_SECONDS. Required facts must be checked and originals recovered while available.
The CLI is supplied by the PyPI distribution. The similarly named npm headroom-ai package is a TypeScript SDK and does not supply the headroom CLI.

The failed content=@file transport shape is not evidence that Headroom cannot accept file contents: its required MCP input is content, while mcporter supports key=@path when the target is selected correctly. File-argument and target-selection contract: https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/docs/cli-reference.md#mcporter-call-servertool .

new_since_pin.text: v0.38.0 includes protection of Bash control flow, byte-exact file-read output through the lossless fold, and accounting changes such as counting compression savings once per conversation. These changes do not constitute an explicit fix for the log omission-count defect.

v0.39.0 adds protect_messages as a compression veto, descriptions of what CCR dropped (#3635), retrievable sentinels for dropped scalar-array items (#3692), and cache-prefix fixes. These are related fidelity features, but the live v0.38.0/v0.39.0 release notes and CHANGELOG contain no explicit fix for the measured log omission notice counting kept lines; the local 0.39.0 qualification itself still found that defect. Do not infer that the switch blocker is resolved from those entries.

Newly released v0.39.1 fixes the 0.39.0 proxy TPM limiter indefinitely refusing large-context requests (#3806). Its release note does not address log omission counts; qualifying the latest candidate against that retained fixture remains necessary. Complete changelog also checked: https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/v0.39.1/CHANGELOG.md .

native_adaptation.how_we_install: Active installation uses CPython 3.13 and the upstream MCP extra: uv tool install --python 3.13 'headroom-ai[mcp]==0.37.0' (recipes/README.md:96 and :494-502). The current portable bootstrap downloads and verifies the pinned platform wheel before uv installs the equivalent headroom-ai[mcp] @ file:// package; dependencies still resolve through uv's index (adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json:263; adoption/bootstrap.md:159). The card records 0.39.0 as staged but not switched; this research does not install or switch either candidate.
native_adaptation.claude_wiring: recipes/README.md:500-505 registers headroom at Claude user scope using the upstream headroom mcp serve command, an unreachable loopback proxy URL http://127.0.0.1:1, and HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1. This selects local on-demand compression/retrieval, with no automatic provider interception. adoption/templates/claude.settings.template.json has no headroom plugin or tool registration, and none of examples/claude-native/agents/*.md explicitly names headroom tools in its allowlist; only isolated-builder.md:4 and evidence-reviewer.md:4 name context-mode ctx_* tools.
native_adaptation.codex_wiring: adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml:55-70 registers headroom directly at user scope with args [mcp, serve, --proxy-url, http://127.0.0.1:1] and all four offline environment guards. It is not routed through mcporter. The live repo .codex/config.toml has no headroom table because this server is at user scope; selected read-only inspection of ~/.codex/config.toml confirmed the same direct launch but only HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1, so the two Hugging Face guards in the newer template have not reached this host's user registration (adoption/bootstrap.md:245; recipes/README.md:505).
native_adaptation.lane_rule: Use Headroom only for selected content that passes fidelity checks; retain originals, call headroom_compress then headroom_retrieve by returned hash, include recovery cost, and do not stack compressors on one artifact (docs/token-session-handbook.md:106-117 and :130; recipes/README.md:507-525). The supplied worker token-lanes block explicitly names Headroom for large selected text. The native recipe states there is no headroom compress CLI subcommand; the operation here is the MCP tool.

deviations_from_upstream.what: Native-stack selects local, on-demand MCP compression with a dead proxy URL instead of upstream's optional automatic traffic proxy.
deviations_from_upstream.why: The retained scope is selected-artifact compression with exact original recovery, not rerouting every Claude/Codex model request (recipes/README.md:507-525; manifests/stack.json:544). This is an upstream-supported MCP mode, not missing installation functionality: https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/v0.39.1/docs/content/docs/mcp.mdx#mcp-only-no-proxy .
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Retain this explicit scope and report complete compression/retrieval cost. Evaluate automatic proxy routing separately only if the intended workload changes; its headline performance is not the measured performance of this adaptation.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The live Codex user registration lacks two offline guards already present in the portable template.
deviations_from_upstream.why: recipes/README.md:505 explains that HEADROOM_OFFLINE's Hugging Face environment setup runs at proxy startup, not headroom mcp serve; the template consequently also sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE. The live selected registration still contains only HEADROOM_OFFLINE and DO_NOT_TRACK. The same recipe separately notes the tiktoken cache requirement, so the four variables should not be described as a blanket guarantee for every tokenizer download.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Bring the host registration into line with adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml:66-70 and preserve the documented pre-populated tiktoken-cache handling when qualifying a cold-cache setup. No host registration was changed here.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The first retained compression command used an incomplete mcporter target-selection shape and failed; a corrected invocation succeeded.
deviations_from_upstream.why: The first card entry uses --name headroom --tool headroom_compress content=@file without --server, and returns exit 1 with content missing. mcporter v0.14.1 src/cli/call-arguments.ts:170-171 consumes the first positional token as selector when server is absent, before parsing named arguments; --name names an ephemeral server but does not supply the parser's --server selection (https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/src/cli/call-arguments.ts#L164). Headroom correctly requires content, and @file itself is supported.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Use the retained successful --server headroom --tool headroom_compress content=@file shape, or a complete server.tool selector with an explicit JSON payload. Preserve the initial failure in the evidence rather than reporting that every upstream command passed.

deviations_from_upstream.what: Installed, explicitly named guidance has not produced any Headroom invocation in the measured lanes-block worker population.
deviations_from_upstream.why: The assembled card reports workflow_children_with_lanes_block mcp_calls 0, cli_calls 0 and agents_using 0 out of agents 22, despite the supplied lanes text naming Headroom. The example-agent allowlists do not explicitly name Headroom tools. This establishes an adoption gap in that population, not a runtime failure or proof that every task needed compression.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Review artifact suitability, access and concrete compress/retrieve examples in intended worker workflows before attributing expected savings to installation or guidance alone; add explicit tool access only for agents intended to use this lane.
